target: fatal accidents involving Boeing commercial jets

evidence.publisher: Ethiopian Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (EAIB); final report hosted by the French BEA
evidence.authority_role: state accident-investigation authority / accredited-representative public host
evidence.source_title: Aircraft Accident Investigation Report B737-MAX 8, ET-AVJ
evidence.observation: The EAIB final report identifies Ethiopian Airlines flight ET302 as a Boeing 737 MAX 8, registration ET-AVJ, scheduled international passenger flight from Addis Ababa to Nairobi on 10 March 2019; all 157 persons on board were fatally injured.

evidence.publisher: Bureau d'Enquêtes et d'Analyses pour la sécurité de l'aviation civile (BEA)
evidence.authority_role: Annex 13 accredited representative and official investigation portal
evidence.source_title: Accident to the Boeing 737 registered ET-AVJ and operated by Ethiopian Airlines on 10/03/2019 near Bishoftu
evidence.observation: BEA identifies Ethiopia-AIB as responsible entity and records the occurrence as an accident involving Ethiopian Airlines Boeing 737 ET-AVJ, commercial air transport passenger operation, with 157 deaths.
IATA reports eight fatal accidents in 2019 and explicitly identifies the Ethiopian Airlines B737 MAX crash in March as a fatal passenger-flight accident with 157 passengers and crew killed.

completeness_assessment.reason: ET302 is supported by the state investigation record and independent IATA annual evidence, but the complete 2019 global fatal-event set has not yet been mapped exhaustively against the fixed Boeing-commercial-jet target.
